correctness.rationale: Every length-n Sturmian factor is one of n+1 irrational rotation cylinder words. Crossing b_j exchanges 01 and 10 for j<n; the exchanged one has rank floor(j alpha)+1. T^k removes this change precisely when j alpha<k. Crossing b_n changes the last bit from 0 to 1 and is always strictly increasing. All remaining crossings strictly raise the images in lex order, so there are n+1-min(n-1,floor(k/alpha)) distinct images and no nonadjacent coincidences. The slope irrationality, endpoint convention, cases with too few ones, k>=1 and n>=1 are explicitly handled. The two finite programs independently check 266253 swaps, 26611 terminal changes and 973080 exact rational mechanical cases; finite tests are not relied upon for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work explicitly asks for Sturmian tortoise complexity, a natural new invariant interpolating between factor and Abelian complexity. This gives a complete formula across every irrational slope, every k and every positive length; it identifies the exact sharp Abelian stabilization threshold instead of approximate behavior or isolated finite examples. The result is structurally explained by a monotone cylinder partition and the ordinal rank of each crossing bit.
